summary: Reproduces the CCITT draft recommendation T.4, the standard for group 3 facsimile encoding. It is useful for compressing bitmap data.

eli5.summary: This is the official rulebook for how fax machines squeeze a page into a short message and unsqueeze it at the other end.

questions: how does fax encoding compress images
how do group 3 fax machines work
what is run-length encoding for fax
subtitle: How fax machines compress pages into streams of bits.

tldr.problem: Facsimile machines need a standard way to represent scanned documents as data to transmit efficiently over telephone lines.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 804 specifies CCITT T.4, a run-length encoding scheme that compresses lines of black and white pixels by representing runs of the same color as variable-length binary codes, reducing transmission time to about one minute per A4 page.
tldr.outcome: This standard became the foundation for Group 3 fax machines worldwide, making document transmission practical and economical for decades.

today: RFC 804 is Historic and no longer the standard for modern fax transmission; it has been superseded by Group 4 (CCITT T.6) which uses more efficient two-dimensional encoding. However, Group 3 fax as defined in T.4 remained in widespread use through the 20th century and some systems still support it for compatibility.

sections.title: Why Fax Machines Need Standards
sections.content:
Fax transmission is about turning a paper document into binary data that a telephone line can carry. The challenge is efficiency: sending every pixel individually would be slow and expensive. The CCITT (International Telegraph and Telephone Consultative Committee) developed Group 3 facsimile as a practical standard for this, building on earlier Groups 1 and 2 that were too slow for widespread office use.

Group 3 aims to transmit a standard ISO A4 page in about one minute over a regular telephone circuit. To achieve this, CCITT T.4 specifies how to scan the page, what resolution to use, how to encode the pixels, and what transmission protocols to follow.
sections.eli5: Before there were rules, different fax machines couldn't talk to each other. T.4 is the rulebook everyone agreed to follow so any fax machine can send a picture to any other one.

sections.title: Scanning and Resolution Standards
sections.content:
Group 3 facsimile defines the physical scanning process: the scanning direction moves left to right and top to bottom, just as humans read. The standard specifies two resolutions: a normal definition of 3.85 lines per millimeter and an optional higher definition of 7.7 lines per millimeter in the vertical direction.

Each scanning line contains 1728 black and white picture elements (pels). The total scanning line length is 215 millimeters, which corresponds to standard A4 paper width (210mm for the image area plus margins). Input documents must be at least ISO A4 size, and the scanning line can be adjusted for other widths while maintaining correct picture proportions.
sections.eli5: A fax divides a page into tiny dots in a grid. The standard says use 1728 dots across, scan from left to right and top to bottom, just like reading a book.

sections.title: Run-Length Encoding
sections.content:
The heart of T.4 is its one-dimensional run-length encoding scheme. Instead of representing each of 1728 pixels individually, the encoder counts consecutive pixels of the same color (white or black) and transmits a single code word representing that run.

Run lengths from 0 to 63 pixels are encoded using Terminating Code words, which have their own tables for white and black runs. Run lengths from 64 to 1728 pixels are encoded as a Make Up Code word (representing a multiple of 64) followed by a Terminating Code word (representing the remainder). This approach reduces the data significantly: a line of all white pixels requires only a few bits instead of thousands.

The encoding rules ensure all lines begin with a white run length code (using zero if the line starts with black), so the receiver can maintain color synchronization. The scheme includes separate tables for extended widths to support larger paper formats.
sections.eli5: Instead of saying '1 white, 1 black, 1 white, 1 black' for a checkerboard, the encoder says '500 alternating white and black pairs' using short codes. It's like shorthand for patterns.

sections.title: Line Endings and Control Signals
sections.content:
Each line of encoded data is followed by an End of Line (EOL) code (binary 000000000001), which serves as a unique marker for resynchronization. If an error occurs during transmission, the receiver can detect the next EOL to recover. An EOL also precedes the first data line of a page.

If transmission timing requirements demand it, FILL (a variable string of zeros) can be inserted between data and EOL to pad the transmission time to the minimum required by the mode in use. Fill may be up to 5 seconds of transmission time, after which the receiver may disconnect.

At the end of a document, Return to Control (RTC) is signaled by six consecutive EOLs, after which the transmitter sends post-message commands in the standard T.30 blocked format.
sections.eli5: The fax adds a special marker (like a period) at the end of each line so the machine knows when one line ends and the next starts, even if something goes wrong.

sections.title: Transmission Timing and Modulation
sections.content:
The total transmission time for a scanning line (data plus fill plus EOL) has a minimum and maximum. The standard recommends 20 milliseconds per line as the standard with an optional fallback to 40 milliseconds, while also recognizing 10 and 5 millisecond options with mandatory fallbacks. The maximum transmission time for any line is less than 5 seconds.

The identification and choice of transmission time is made during the pre-message (Phase B) portion of the T.30 control procedure between sender and receiver. Group 3 apparatus uses modulation methods defined in CCITT Recommendation V.27ter at data signalling rates of 4800 or 2400 bits per second. For higher-speed operation on leased circuits, V.29 modulation is provisionally agreed to be usable.
sections.eli5: Different phone lines have different speeds, so the fax machines agree beforehand on how fast to send data. They can use methods that work over regular phone lines or faster methods for dedicated lines.

items.label: Terminating Codes
items.desc: Represents white or black runs of 0 to 63 pels. Each color has its own table of variable-length binary codes.

items.label: Make Up + Terminating
items.desc: For longer runs, a Make Up Code represents 64–1728 in multiples, followed by a Terminating Code for the remainder.

items.label: End of Line
items.desc: Unique marker at the end of each scanned line, enables resynchronization after transmission errors.
